chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Ali ibn Asbat from his uncle Ya'qub ibn Salim from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), who said:

There are three - whoever does not have them, his goodness can never be hoped for: he who does not fear Allah in private, he who does not become pious at old age, and he who is not ashamed of his faults.

key_terms.الشيب: Grey hair/old age - symbolizing the urgency to reform before death
key_terms.الغيب: The unseen/private - acting righteously even when no one watches

ai.seo_question: What three traits indicate hopelessness according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies three essential character traits whose absence means a person's goodness is beyond hope: fearing Allah when unobserved (taqwa in private), reforming oneself upon reaching old age (self-correction before death), and feeling shame for one's own faults (moral consciousness). This was directed at the general Muslim community as a standard for self-evaluation.
